messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: spike in errors and latency on POST /v1/embeddings (us-east-1). Observed: 4xx (dim-mismatch), 5xx (runtime batching), and doubled billing chargebacks. Trigger at 2026-03-15T18:45:45Z
Raj (oncall): ack. Assigning Priya + Carlos + billing. Zoe, any customer reports?
Zoe (support): multiple tickets from two customers: one reports failed nightly ingest with \"embedding dimension mismatch expected 1536 got 512\". Another reports intermittent 500s with long tails. Both started ~18:30 UTC after a deploy. They also flagged unexpected higher billing for the window (lots of retries).
Priya (eng-ml): did we rotate any embed model aliases or push quantized variants today?
Carlos (eng-runtime): there was a canary deploy to change batching heuristics at 18:28. Rollout was partial. I'm pulling runtime traces now.
Zoe (support): sample customer request (anonymized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"embed-stable-alias\",\"input\":[\"p1\",\"p2\",\"p3\",\"p4\"],\"batch_size\":4}'
```
Response: `400 Bad Request - embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 512`
Priya (eng-ml): embedding sizes 1536 vs 512 — looks like a small-variant got mixed into alias. Which variants are behind alias?
Carlos (eng-runtime): alias mapping: embed-stable-alias -> [embed-1536-v2 (85%), embed-512-quant (15%)]. The quant variant was added last week for cost tests. The batching change coalesces small requests and sometimes routes to any available variant causing mixed-dim batches.
Raj (oncall): ok that's the vector. Consequence: when requests are co-batched across variants, we fail dim validation or run inference on wrong kernel creating 500s. Also retries were auto-issued by SDKs leading to double billing.
Marta (billing): we see a burst of chargeable token events tied to /v1/embeddings with response codes 4xx and 5xx during the incident window. We need to capture customer ids for credits.
Priya (eng-ml): immediate mitigation suggestions:
- remove embed-512-quant from alias (config flip).
- revert batching heuristic change (fast rollback).
- add runtime guard that enforces per-batch dim homogeneity before co-batching.
Carlos (eng-runtime): I can flip alias to 100% embed-1536-v2 now. Also reverting the batching change (rollback id: batch-heuristic-2026-03-15) will take ~2m.
Raj (oncall): do it. Also add a temporary header-based bypass for customers that want to pin to 1536 model: `X-Model-Pin: embed-1536-v2` — Zoe, can you surface to affected customers?
Carlos (eng-runtime): applied alias flip, invalidated local caches. Kicking rollback of batching heuristic.
deploy-bot: rollback job batch-heuristic-2026-03-15 initiated... complete.
(oncall-bot): metric update: /v1/embeddings 400 errors down 92% in 4m, 5xx down 90%, p95 latency reduced from 2.4s to 320ms.
Zoe (support): customer A confirms bulk ingest resumed. They asked for a formal explanation and a credit.
Marta (billing): noted. I'll open a billing investigation and propose issuing a pro-rated credit for the affected window. Requesting list of API keys and timestamps. Zoe, please attach ticket ids.
Priya (eng-ml): root cause hypothesis: alias included a quantized 512 variant for cost testing; new co-batching heuristic promoted higher mixing of requests across variants leading to cross-variant co-batches; the runtime didn't validate dims prior to co-batching. Edge-case: small batch_size combined with larger ones caused 512-vector requests to be co-batched with 1536 ones.
Carlos (eng-runtime): immediate code-level fix: add dim-check in co-batch planner and fail-safe to split batches by model variant. I'll open a hotfix PR (owner: Carlos). Tests: add integration that simulates mixed-variant traffic. ETA for PR: 6 hours.
Raj (oncall): action items recap:
- runtime: dim pre-check + split fallback (Carlos)
- model/router: remove quant variant from alias until compatibility testing done (Carlos/Priya)
- support: notify customers + provide X-Model-Pin header workaround (Zoe)
- billing: identify impacted keys + issue credits (Marta)
- postmortem: schedule and include canary test matrix (Raj)
Zoe (support): I'll post an update to affected customers with workaround and ETA for fix.
Marta (billing): collecting keys now. Will share CSV to internal channel.
Carlos (eng-runtime): opened PR #3821 with tests, adding dim check and single-item fallback. Starting canary roll after code review.
Priya (eng-ml): also adding a model-compatibility matrix to the alias publish workflow so future additions must declare embedding_dim metadata and auto-reject incompatible variants.
Raj (oncall): tracking incident severity: P2 -> will keep open until fix in prod and billing credits processed. Logging incident tag: embeddings, alias-routing, batching, billing-impact.
Zoe (support): customer B had SDK retries turned on; suggest we add guidance to SDK: do not retry on 4xx dim-mismatch errors. I'll open a ticket to update SDK retry logic.
Carlos (eng-runtime): canary shows no regressions. Scheduling full rollout in 1h unless we see new errors.
(oncall-bot): metrics stable for 18m. 2 customers impacted confirmed.
Raj (oncall): closing active pageing. moving state to mitigated. We'll run postmortem tomorrow 11:00 PT.
Zoe (support): leaving final note in tickets with apologies, workaround, and credit pledge.
Marta (billing): will propose credits by EOD.
